title: Q-STD-w3c-prov: serve the public changelog as W3C PROV-O JSON-LD
body:
**Owner:** executor
**Trigger:** executor tick, driver order
**Done check:** cmd:python3 -m foundation standards --adopted w3c-prov
**Status:** open

The public changelog (foundation/provenance.py `public_view`, ops/changelog.json, /changelog) holds who changed what: origin class and actor, kind, summary, affected paths, effect. Add one mapping function that renders those public rows as PROV-O in JSON-LD (`@context` https://www.w3.org/ns/prov: each row a prov:Activity with prov:startedAtTime, prov:wasAssociatedWith a prov:Agent for origin.actor typed by origin class, and prov:used / prov:generated prov:Entity for each affected path) and serve it at /changelog.jsonld from the same data the page shows. Private rows never leave the ledger (the same redaction as `public_view`). Test: parse the output, every node has an @id and an @type from the PROV namespace, and the number of activities equals the number of public rows. Register the surface and set the register row to supported with the test.

STANDARDS-FIRST-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-25): "Standards, don't reinvent the wheel. Apply standards." The row is `w3c-prov` in seed/standards/standards.json; this item closes when that row reads `"adoption": "adopted"` and every probe on it passes. Change the row in the same change that makes it true, never before.
